conclusion.sember: the only S-EMBER-FITTED constant in the suite is confidence-cascade's recall confidence floor, and amendment 2 fits it on the DEV split. The committed S-EMBER recall-accuracy table (`recall_profiles.py`) is read by no arm - only by the report generator - so no arm carries a constant fitted on the full question set. Every per-question device-answer probability a policy reads is a MEASUREMENT of that question, not a constant fitted across questions, and the harness supplies it only to the arms whose published mechanism observes the device's answer.
conclusion.nexar: every FITTED episodic tunable in the suite (every router, every score quantile, every window selection) comes from `devsplit`, which is StudyD3's DEVELOPMENT clips. NOT fitted but MEASURED ON THE EVALUATION CLIPS, and listed here as the amendment requires: the resource-quality profile (`profiles.stream_profile`: quality from StudyE9b / E9c, lag from StudyE9b's hold shift, demand from StudyE9 / E9b) and StudyE9d's V(d) and d* curves, all measured on StudyD14b's 300 validation clips. They are inputs to videostorm, eco-llm, inar-vl, perllm, B3, B6, B8, B9 and B10. This is the suite's documented ADAPTATION A2 (the paper profiles online; we substitute a measured profile), and it is a KNOWN leak of evaluation-clip information into a decision rule, reported and not fixed: re-measuring the profile on StudyD3's development clips needs GPU time.
